title: Microsoft Teams: choose the institution type in the Teams for Education Policy Wizard
summary: Hold: the briefing treats licensing as unpublished even though Microsoft documents the Teams for Education licensing prerequisite. Its claim that policies change only when an administrator selects Apply also overlooks Microsoft's documented automatic updates after the wizard has run.

claims.claim: Administrators can select their institution's tenant type in the policy wizard and change it later.
claims.quote: Admins can now select tenant type for their institution from the policy wizard. This setting can be changed anytime from the wizard.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2024.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2024"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and does not list other clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Desktop, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.claim: The record identifies Microsoft Teams as the product.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.claim: The wizard's educational institution type options are Primary or Secondary and Higher education.
claims.quote: The wizard sets up policies based on educational institution type (Primary or Secondary or Higher education).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The wizard adjusts Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions for students according to institution type.
claims.quote: Students: The wizard adjusts the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition of each policy area covered by the wizard with new default settings that are appropriate to keep your students safe.

claims.claim: The wizard creates custom policy definitions for educators and staff.
claims.quote: Educators and staff: The wizard creates a set of custom policy definitions for each policy area covered by the wizard with settings tailored to the needs of educators and staff.

claims.claim: The custom policies are assigned to the educators and staff groups the administrator selects.
claims.quote: Educators and staff in the groups you select will be assigned a set of custom policies tailored to their needs.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The wizard accepts up to three educators and staff groups.
claims.quote: You can select up to three groups.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The seven student policy areas are Teams, Meeting, Live events, App setup, App permission, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote: Students: Teams policy ... Meeting policy ... Live events policy ... App setup policy ... App permission policy ... Messaging policy ... Calling policy

claims.claim: The five educator and staff custom policy areas are Teams, Meeting, Live events, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote:
Teams policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Teams
Meeting policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Meeting
Live events policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Live events
Messaging policy | Primary or Secondary Educators and Staff - Messaging
Calling policy

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The administrator can rerun the wizard to change institution type, educator and staff groups, or both.
claims.quote: You can change your institution type, the groups of educators and staff to which you want to assign policies, or both.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Changing only institution type applies the new type's Global policy definitions to students.
claims.quote: Change only the educational institution type | - Students: The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions based on the new educational institution type are applied to students.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Changing only institution type creates and assigns new custom definitions to the educators and staff groups.
claims.quote: Educators and staff: A set of custom policy definitions based on the new educational institution type is created and assigned to the educators and staff groups.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Changing institution type removes the previous type's custom policy definitions from the educators and staff groups.
claims.quote: The custom policy definitions created for the previous educational institution type are removed from the educators and staff groups.

claims.claim: After the wizard has run, the education default for a new Teams feature is added to Global policies without administrator intervention.
claims.quote: Also, whenever a new feature is added to Teams, the appropriate EDU relevant default value of the policy for that feature will be automatically added to the Global (Org-wide default) without requiring any admin intervention.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes student policies as more restrictive than educator and staff policies.
claims.quote: Policies for students need to be more restrictive to reduce their risk of receiving inappropriate levels of access. Educators and staff need a separate set of policies that can be more permissive to enable them to be successful.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Existing direct and group assignments must be removed from students for the wizard's Global definitions to take effect.
claims.quote: Remove all existing direct assignments and group assignments from your students so that the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition applied by the wizard takes effect.

claims.claim: The wizard assigns educator and staff group policies at ranking 1, the highest ranking.
claims.quote: Keep in mind that the wizard assigns policies to your educators and staff group using a group assignment ranking of 1, which is the highest ranking.

claims.claim: An existing same-area policy assigned to the educators and staff group is moved to a lower ranking.
claims.quote: If your educators and staff group has an existing policy of the same policy area assigned to it, that existing policy is moved to a lower ranking and the policy assigned by the wizard takes effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Conflicting direct assignments override the wizard's educator and staff group policies and must be removed.
claims.quote: Remove any conflicting direct assignments for your educators and staff so that the custom policy definition created by the wizard takes effect.

claims.claim: Initial application of the wizard's selected policies is administrator opt-in and requires selecting Apply.
claims.quote: Select Apply to apply your changes.

claims.claim: The wizard starts automatically for administrators who are new to Teams.
claims.quote: If you're new to Teams, the wizard automatically starts.

claims.claim: Applying the wizard changes may take a few minutes, with Global definitions applied to students at that step.
claims.quote: Select Apply to apply your changes. This may take a few minutes to complete.The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions are immediately applied to students.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Educator and staff custom policy assignment can take a few hours depending on group size.
claims.quote: For your educators and staff, it could take a few hours for the custom policies to be assigned to each member of the groups you selected, depending on the size of the groups.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The first-run wizard is reached in the Microsoft Teams admin center through Home > Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment > Quick setup.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Home, and then in the Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment tile, select Quick setup.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the wizard's initial institution-type selection is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams institution type PowerShell wizard; Teams institution type Graph; Teams institution type Graph beta. Read easy-policy-setup-edu, Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration and Teams Graph overview search excerpts; no matching operation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The rerun wizard is reached in the Microsoft Teams admin center through Home > Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment > Change.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Home, and then in the Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment tile, select Change.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Graph operation to change or read the wizard's institution type is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams institution type PowerShell wizard; Teams institution type Graph; Teams institution type Graph beta. Read easy-policy-setup-edu, Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration and Teams Graph overview excerpts; no matching operation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The wizard's own Learn page and the roadmap record name no licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard license. Read the complete easy-policy-setup-edu page and roadmap record; neither names a licence. Also read teams-edu-licensing and the Teams for Education prerequisite page for the broader licensing claim.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page names no administrator role required to run it.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard role. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full; it names no required role. Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration specifies a role for that cmdlet, not for running this wizard.

claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page and roadmap record name no meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard meter price. Read easy-policy-setup-edu and the roadmap record; neither names a meter. Read teams-edu-licensing for product licensing context.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published which licence covers this wizard.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites for Microsoft Teams for Education
- An Education license in your Microsoft 365 tenant
- Enable Microsoft Teams in the Microsoft Admin Center
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and replace the blanket unpublished-licensing statements with: 'Teams for Education requires an Education license in the Microsoft 365 tenant. Microsoft lists Teams as part of the free Microsoft 365 A1 for Students SKU. The wizard page states no separate wizard-specific licence requirement.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/education/guide/2-baseline/applications/baseline-apps-teams-what-is-teams and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-edu-licensing. In Open questions, remove the broad licence question or narrow it to a separate wizard-specific requirement. Retain the low cost rating for administration time.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration has no institution-type parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams institution type Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration. Read the full cited cmdlet reference: parameters are ParentGuardianPreferredContactMethod, UpdateParentInformation, EduGenerativeAIEnhancements, Identity, WhatIf, Confirm and common parameters.

claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page does not say when institution-type selection was added.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard institution type added. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full; it describes selection and rerunning but gives no date for introducing type selection.

claims.claim: The sources do not say existing policies change if nobody runs the wizard.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard without run. Read easy-policy-setup-edu and the roadmap record; the documented changes follow running the wizard, and neither describes policy changes before an administrator runs it.

claims.claim: The wizard documentation describes no new data access mechanism.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard data access. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full; it describes policy definitions and assignments, not a new data access mechanism.

claims.claim: Learn describes replacement custom definitions rather than carrying edits on the previous type's definitions into the new type.
claims.quote: A set of custom policy definitions based on the new educational institution type is created and assigned to the educators and staff groups. The custom policy definitions created for the previous educational institution type are removed from the educators and staff groups.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators without educators and staff groups to create a group and rerun the wizard.
claims.quote: If you don't have any groups set up yet for your educators and staff, create a group, and then rerun the wizard.

claims.claim: The wizard offers a review step before Apply.
claims.quote:
4. Review your selections.
5. Select Apply to apply your changes.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends checking Message center for new Teams features and policy settings.
claims.quote: But do check the Message Center (in the Microsoft 365 admin center) frequently to stay up to date on new features and their policies and policy settings in Teams.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The wizard acts, and policies change, only when an administrator selects Apply.
claims.quote: Also, whenever a new feature is added to Teams, the appropriate EDU relevant default value of the policy for that feature will be automatically added to the Global (Org-wide default) without requiring any admin intervention.
claims.fix: Replace 'The wizard acts only when an admin selects Apply' with 'The initial policy application requires an admin to select Apply; after that, Microsoft says education defaults for new Teams features are added to Global policies automatically.' In the risk rationale replace 'Policies change only when an admin selects Apply in the wizard' with 'Initial policy application requires an admin to select Apply; later education defaults can be added automatically'. Keep the existing defaultState and low risk rating: the initial configuration remains opt-in.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to remove policy assignments, but the controls table contains only institution-type selection rows.
claims.quote: Remove existing assignments as Learn's after-wizard steps instruct: for students, existing direct and group assignments; for educators and staff, conflicting direct assignments. | Institution type chosen on the first run of the wizard | Institution type changed after the wizard has run
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout bullet beginning 'Remove existing assignments as Learn's after-wizard steps instruct'. Retain the Before rollout instruction to review the documentation's after-run instructions and the accurate explanation in Risk assessment; do not add control rows.
